title: Call for Articles: “Marketing Without the Marketer?”
details_text:
About the Opportunity:
Marque, the Marketing Club of IIM Rohtak, invites you to feature your article in the upcoming edition of its monthly magazine, Insights.
This edition explores " Marketing Without the Marketer? ", examining how artificial intelligence is reshaping the creative and strategic core of marketing itself.
As AI tools generate copy, visuals, campaigns, and even personalized brand communication within seconds, the boundaries of human creativity, authenticity, and skill in marketing are being redefined. From questions of authorship and originality to consumers' ability to distinguish real from generated content, brands are increasingly navigating a landscape where the human touch is no longer a given. This edition explores what AI means for creativity, authenticity, and the evolving skillset of the modern marketer.
Themes:
Who Made This Ad?
AI tools can now generate copy, visuals, and even entire campaigns within seconds, raising questions about where human creativity fits in the process. Explore how the role of the marketer is evolving, from creator to curator, editor, or director, and whether AI-assisted work diminishes or elevates the craft of marketing.
Authenticity in an AI World
As AI becomes capable of mimicking human tone, emotion, and personalization at scale, the line between genuine and generated communication continues to blur. Discuss whether consumers can tell the difference, or even care, and what this shift means for how brands build and sustain authenticity.
The New Marketing Skillset
As AI takes over execution-heavy tasks, the skills that define a good marketer are being redefined. Examine how prompt engineering, creative direction, and strategic judgment are becoming as important as traditional marketing skills, and what capabilities will separate marketers who thrive from those who get left behind.
As AI continues to blur the lines between human and machine-made marketing, brands and marketers alike must navigate a landscape where creativity, authenticity, and skill are being redefined in real time. We invite you to explore what it truly means to market in an AI-first world, and what the future holds for the humans behind the brand.
Share your insights. Shape the conversation.
Submission Guidelines:
Submit an article under any one of the three themes
Mention the selected sub-theme at the beginning of your article and include a title for your article
The article should be between 800 and 1,000 words
Font: Times New Roman
Font Size: 12
Submissions outside the prescribed themes will be disqualified
Any form of plagiarism will lead to disqualification
On the first page, include:
A short author bio (30–50 words)
A passport-size photograph
Name of your institution
Email ID

LinkedIn profile link
UPI ID (for prize money disbursement)
Images without a source or label will not be accepted
Rules:

Only college students are eligible to participate

Submissions must be made in .doc or .docx format through Unstop only

details_text:
Overview

About the Competition
Pirates of the Portfolio is FISCUL’s flagship finance competition , organised as part of EconVista 2026 , the Department of Economics’ annual academic fest. The competition is designed to take participants beyond conventional finance quizzes and test their ability to apply financial knowledge, analyse problems, and make decisions under pressure.
The competition progresses through multiple stages, beginning with an online preliminary quiz, followed by an online finance case challenge, and culminating in a live stock-market simulation and investment pitch .
The quiz will test participants across financial markets, corporate finance, and current affairs, while also assessing their logical reasoning, mathematical aptitude, arithmetic skills, and analytical thinking.
The final stage will place teams in the role of fund managers , where they will have to respond to changing market conditions, manage their portfolios, and make investment decisions in real time. The competition will ultimately test not just what participants know about finance, but how effectively they can apply it when the stakes are high.
Competition Format
Round 1: Preliminary Quiz - An online quiz testing participants across financial markets, corporate finance, current affairs, logical reasoning, mathematical aptitude, arithmetic, and other core financial concepts. Each question will have a different maximum score based on its difficulty, with the 10 questions adding up to 1,000 points.For each question, teams can bet any number of points up to its maximum, based on their confidence. Correct answers earn the points wagered, while incorrect answers lose them. Teams will be ranked based on their final score, with the highest-scoring teams advancing to the next round.
Round 2: Finance Case Challenge - An online case challenge where shortlisted teams will be presented with a real-world finance problem. Teams will be required to analyse the situation, identify the key issues, work with the information and data provided, and develop a practical and well-reasoned recommendation.The strongest 8 teams will qualify for the on-campus final round.
Final Round: Live Stock Market Simulation - The final round will take place on-campus at Lady Shri Ram College for Women and will consist of two stages.
Stage 1: Stock Market Simulation The top 8 teams will participate in a live stock-market simulation, acting as fund managers with an initial virtual capital of ₹1,00,000.Teams will trade a predefined set of stocks across multiple rounds as market news and developments unfold. With each news update influencing stock prices, teams will have to make strategic buy/sell decisions while managing risk and maximising their portfolio value.The top 5 teams from the simulation will advance to the final stage.
Stage 2: Shark Tank Window The top 5 teams will pitch their investment strategy to a panel of judges acting as Sharks. Teams will have a short window to present their investment strategy, best trade/investment thesis, key risks, and why the Sharks should back them.The Sharks will have a separate pool of capital and can choose to invest in teams whose strategies they believe in.
Eligibility & Team Formation
Open to students of all years and academic backgrounds.
Teams must consist of 1–4 members.
Cross-college team participation is permitted.
Rules & Guidelines
All submissions must be made within the officially communicated submission window. No extensions will be provided.
Teams have creative freedom in their case submissions and pitches, provided the substance of their analysis remains clear.
The final round will be conducted in person at Lady Shri Ram College for Women, Delhi.
The decision of the judges will be final and binding.

Genie X Hub Presents: PROJECT ECLIPSE HACKATHON
Build AI That Thinks, Acts & Automates — Not Just Answers.
Project Eclipse Hackathon is a hybrid AI-focused hackathon by Genie Hive Private Limited , designed for college students, developers, AI enthusiasts, designers, and innovators who want to build practical solutions using Generative AI, Agentic AI, Autonomous Systems, and Intelligent Automation .
This is more than a conventional chatbot-building competition. Participants are challenged to build systems that can understand problems, reason, use tools and APIs, execute actions, verify outcomes, and involve humans when necessary .

THE ECLIPSE CHALLENGE
AI is moving beyond systems that simply generate responses.
Project Eclipse focuses on systems that follow the workflow:
INPUT → UNDERSTAND → PLAN → USE TOOLS → ACT → VERIFY → RECOVER / ESCALATE
Participants are encouraged to build working AI systems that solve meaningful problems and demonstrate real task completion rather than simply generating convincing text.
CHALLENGE TRACKS
Participants can choose one of five curated challenges or participate in the OPEN-X Open Innovation Challenge .
01 — AI Agent for Production Incident Investigation & Recovery
Build an autonomous production-operations agent that investigates a simulated production incident across application logs, infrastructure metrics, deployment history, Git commits, alerts, and service dependencies.
The system should demonstrate capabilities such as:
• Multi-source investigation
• Tool/API calling
• Reasoning over temporal events
• Root-cause hypothesis generation
• Confidence estimation
• Remediation planning
• Human approval for high-impact actions
• Recovery verification
• Post-incident report generation
02 — Autonomous Resolution of Cross-System Transaction Mismatches
Build an AI agent that investigates transaction mismatches across invoices, payment records, purchase orders, emails, spreadsheets, and accounting/ERP systems.
The system should be able to:
• Ingest data from multiple sources
• Match transactions/entities
• Retrieve supporting evidence
• Classify discrepancies using context
• Detect partial, duplicate, or missing payments
• Recommend appropriate actions
• Maintain an auditable action trail
• Use human approval for consequential updates
03 — From Contract Language to Executable Business Actions
Build an AI agent that converts contracts into executable compliance workflows.
Your system should be able to:
• Extract obligations
• Identify responsible parties and deadlines
• Reason over conditional clauses
• Generate tasks and workflows
• Send reminders and escalations
• Maintain compliance records
• Handle document hierarchy and amendments
• Resolve conflicts between contract documents and instructions
04 — Autonomous Requirement-to-Quotation Procurement System
Build an AI procurement agent that takes a natural-language purchase requirement and analyzes vendor quotations.
The system should:
• Understand requirements
• Parse quotations from documents, emails, or structured files
• Normalize specifications
• Check mandatory constraints
• Compare cost and trade-offs
• Detect anomalies
• Simulate vendor clarification/negotiation
• Prepare a recommendation for human approval
The goal is not simply to identify the cheapest quotation, but to determine whether a quotation actually satisfies the required specifications.
05 — Issue-to-Pull-Request AI Engineering Agent
Build an AI software-engineering agent that receives a repository, issue description, and acceptance criteria and takes the problem from:
ISSUE → INVESTIGATION → IMPLEMENTATION → TESTING → PULL REQUEST
The agent should demonstrate:
• Repository exploration
• Issue and acceptance-criteria understanding
• Technical hypothesis formation
• Code modification
• Test execution
• Failure analysis and iteration
• Patch/PR generation
• Human review before deployment
OPEN-X — OPEN INNOVATION
Have your own problem worth solving?
Build beyond the brief.
In OPEN-X , participants can define their own real-world problem and build an original solution using Generative AI, Agentic AI, Autonomous Workflows, or Intelligent Automation .

title: Bharat Business Cases: Submit Case Study
details_text:
Bharat Business Cases:
Real Indian Businesses. Real Challenges. Real Marketing Lessons.
A MarkHub24 Case Documentation Initiative:
India's most interesting business stories are not always found in boardrooms of large corporations.
They exist in neighbourhood markets, family-run enterprises, regional brands, local retailers, cafés, manufacturers, service businesses, startups, traditional businesses and emerging ventures across the country.
With Bharat Business Cases , MarkHub24 aims to document these businesses and turn their real-world journeys into structured learning cases for students, marketers, entrepreneurs and business enthusiasts.
We are inviting students, researchers, marketing enthusiasts, aspiring consultants, entrepreneurs and young professionals to identify and document a real Indian business and analyse it through a strong business and marketing lens .
What Is Bharat Business Cases?:
Bharat Business Cases is a MarkHub24 initiative dedicated to documenting real businesses operating across India.
The objective is not simply to tell a business story.
The objective is to understand:
What problem did the business face?
Who are its customers?
What makes the business different?
How does it compete?
How has it built customer relationships?
What marketing strategies does it use?
How has it adapted to changing consumer behaviour?
What challenges has it encountered?
What can other businesses and marketers learn from it?
Each selected submission will be developed as a structured business case and published on the MarkHub24 website , with due credit to the contributor.
Who Can Participate?:
The Call Is Open To:
Undergraduate students.
MBA/PGDM students.
Postgraduate students.
Research scholars.
Marketing enthusiasts.
Business enthusiasts.
Entrepreneurs.
Young professionals.
Independent researchers.
Aspiring consultants.
Anyone interested in studying Indian businesses.
You may participate individually or as a team, subject to the submission requirements.
What Kind Of Businesses Can You Study?:
We are particularly interested in real, operating Indian businesses across different sectors and geographies.
Local & Traditional Businesses:
Neighbourhood retailers.
Family-owned businesses.
Traditional stores.
Local manufacturers.
Wholesalers.
Artisans and craft businesses.
Legacy businesses.
Food & Hospitality:
Local restaurants.
Cafés.
Bakeries.
Sweet shops.
Cloud kitchens.
Street-food businesses.
Regional food brands.
Services:
Coaching institutes.
Salons.
Fitness businesses.
Healthcare-related businesses.
Professional services.
Local agencies.
Education businesses.
Modern & Emerging Businesses:
D2C brands.
Digital-first businesses.
Local startups.
Regional brands.
Social-media-driven businesses.
Technology-enabled local businesses.
MSMEs & Other Businesses:
Manufacturing businesses.
Distributors.
B2B businesses.
Export-oriented businesses.
Family enterprises.
Regional businesses.
The business does not need to be famous or large .
In fact, we encourage participants to look beyond well-known brands and discover businesses whose strategies, adaptations and customer relationships can provide meaningful learning.
What Are We Looking For?:
The most important requirement is that the submission should be based on a real business .
Your case should go beyond publicly available information and generic descriptions.
We want you to investigate and understand the business.
You May Conduct:
Interviews with the owner/founder/manager.
Primary research.
Customer observations.
Business visits.
Secondary research.
Social media analysis.
Website and digital presence analysis.
Competitor analysis.
Market observation.
The final case should demonstrate actual research and marketing thinking .
Marketing Analysis Is Mandatory:
This is a business case with a strong marketing perspective .
Your submission should meaningfully analyse the business's marketing dimensions.
Depending on the business, you may examine:
Customer:
Target customers.
Customer segments.
Consumer behaviour.
Customer needs and motivations.
Buying patterns.
Customer relationships.
Positioning & Branding:
Brand identity.
Positioning.
Value proposition.
Differentiation.
Brand perception.
Local brand equity.
Marketing Strategy:
Product/service strategy.
Pricing.
Distribution.
Promotion.
Customer acquisition.
Retention strategies.
Digital & Social Media:
Social media presence.
Digital marketing.
Content strategy.
WhatsApp marketing.
Online reviews.
Website/e-commerce presence.
Digital customer acquisition.
Competitive Environment:
Key competitors.
Local vs national competition.
Competitive advantage.
Market changes.
Threats and opportunities.
Consumer & Cultural Context:
Local consumer behaviour.
Cultural factors.
Community influence.
Regional preferences.
Changing consumer expectations.
Growth & Adaptation:
Expansion.
New products/services.
Digital transformation.
Changing business models.
Response to market disruptions.
Generational transition.
You do not have to force every framework into your case. Choose the areas that genuinely apply to the business.
Suggested Case Format:
Submissions should be approximately 3,000–4,000 words .
A strong submission may follow this structure:
Case Title:
Create a clear and engaging title that captures the central business or marketing challenge.
Business At A Glance:
Provide basic information such as:
Business name.
Location.
Industry/category.
Year established.
Nature of business.
Approximate scale, where information can be shared.
Founder/owner, where relevant.
3. Business Background:
Tell us how the business started, its evolution, its products/services and its current position.
4. The Market Context:
Explain the market in which the business operates.
Discuss relevant:
Market trends.
Customer behaviour.
Competition.
Local dynamics.
Industry changes.
5. The Business Challenge / Opportunity:
Identify the central challenge, decision or opportunity that makes this business worth studying.
For example:
Declining footfall.
Competition from online platforms.
Changing consumer preferences.
Need for digital transformation.
Expansion into new markets.
Pricing pressure.
Brand repositioning.
Customer retention.
Scaling a traditional business.
6. Marketing Strategy:
This should be the core of the case.
Analyse how the business attracts, serves and retains customers.
Discuss relevant aspects of:
STP | Branding | Positioning | Marketing Mix | Digital Marketing | Consumer Behaviour | Customer Experience | Communication | Distribution | Pricing | Growth Strategy
Use frameworks only where they genuinely help explain the business.
7. What The Business Did:
Document the actual actions taken by the business.
Avoid turning this into hypothetical recommendations.
The focus should be on what the business actually did, why it did it and what happened afterward.
8. Results / Outcomes:
Where information is available, discuss measurable or observable outcomes.
Examples:
Customer growth.
Revenue growth.
Store expansion.
Digital engagement.
Increased enquiries.
New markets.
Repeat customers.
Product expansion.
Improved visibility.
If exact financial figures are confidential, do not disclose them.
9. Marketing Analysis:
Interpret the case through a marketer's perspective.
What strategic decisions appear significant?
What consumer insight can be identified?
What differentiates the business?
What marketing principles can be observed?
10. Key Learnings:
Conclude with practical lessons that students, marketers and entrepreneurs can take from the case.
Verification & Business Consent — Mandatory:
Because Bharat Business Cases is based on real businesses, every selected case will undergo a verification process before publication .
Participants must therefore have a genuine connection with the business or be able to contact an appropriate representative.
Before publication, MarkHub24 will contact the business/owner/founder/authorised representative to verify the case and obtain consent for publication.
Consent must be provided through email.
The business representative should confirm by email that:
The business has been accurately represented to the best of their knowledge.
They have reviewed the relevant case information.
They consent to MarkHub24 publishing the case on its website.
They understand that the case will be published for educational and informational purposes.
Any confidential information that should not be published has been identified or removed.
No case will be published without successful business verification and publication consent.
MarkHub24 may contact the business directly using publicly available or participant-provided contact information.
Photograph Requirement:
Every submission must include at least one clear photograph of the business .
The photograph should preferably show:
The business/store/establishment.
Exterior signage.
Business premises.
Product/service environment.
Owner/founder with the business, where possible.
The photograph should be original or properly authorised for use .
Do not submit copyrighted images downloaded from Google, social media or other websites unless you have permission to use them.
Additional photographs may be included where relevant.
Important Authenticity Requirements:
Participants must ensure that:
The business actually exists and operates in India.
Information presented in the case is factually accurate.
Interviews and statements are represented honestly.
No fabricated business information is used.
No confidential information is disclosed without permission.
Any secondary information is properly researched.
Photographs are authentic and authorised for use.
The submission is original.
AI tools may be used for research assistance, editing or language refinement, but the underlying research, observations, interviews and analysis must be genuine.
A submission that is substantially fabricated, plagiarised or based on an imaginary business will not be considered for publication.
What Happens After Submission?:
Submissions will go through an editorial review process.
The process broadly includes:
Submission → Editorial Screening → Case Review → Business Verification → Consent → Editorial Refinement → Publication
MarkHub24 may contact selected contributors for:
Clarifications.
Additional information.
Supporting photographs.
Business contact details.
Source verification.
Corrections.
Editorial changes.
Selection for publication is subject to editorial review and successful business verification .
Submission does not automatically guarantee publication.
Publication On MarkHub24:
Selected and verified cases will be published on the MarkHub24 website under Bharat Business Cases .
Every published case will carry due credit to the contributor(s) .
Depending on the case and editorial requirements, the published article may include:
Contributor Name | Institution/Organisation | Business Studied | Case Title
MarkHub24 may make reasonable editorial changes to structure, grammar, formatting, headings and presentation while retaining the substance of the contributor's work.
Publication Certificate:
Contributors whose cases are successfully selected, verified and published will receive a MarkHub24 Publication Certificate recognising their contribution to the Bharat Business Cases initiative.
The certificate will acknowledge the contributor's role in researching and documenting a real Indian business case.
Why Participate?:
This is an opportunity to:
Work on a real-world business case.
Conduct primary and secondary research.
Understand Indian consumer behaviour.
Apply marketing frameworks to an actual business.
Build a published portfolio.
Get your work published on MarkHub24.
Receive due credit for your contribution.
Receive a publication certificate.
Develop a case that can strengthen your academic or professional portfolio.
Most importantly, you will contribute to documenting real Indian businesses that are rarely represented in conventional business case literature.
Submission Deadline:
2 October 2026
Submissions received after the deadline may not be considered.
Before You Submit:
Please ensure that you have:
Selected a real Indian business.
Conducted genuine research.
Included a meaningful marketing analysis.
Prepared a 3,000–4,000 word case.
Included at least one original/authorised photograph.
Provided accurate business information.
Obtained the necessary information from the business.
Kept confidential information protected.
Provided appropriate business contact details for verification.
Ensured the case is original.
The Central Question:
Don't ask only:
“What is this business?”
Ask:
“Why does this business work, how does it compete, how does it understand its customers, and what can marketers learn from it?”
That is what Bharat Business Cases is about.
Real Indian Businesses.
Real Business Challenges.
Real Marketing Lessons.
Submit your case by 2 October 2026 and help us document the businesses that shape India's markets, one case at a time.
Organised By MarkHub24:
The Marketing Intelligence & Learning Ecosystem

title: The Corporate Heist 1.0 | The Forensic Investigation Case Competition
details_text:
Overview
Think you can spot a lie in a spreadsheet? Prove it.
The Corporate Heist is a three-round forensic investigation competition where a company that looked unstoppable falls apart, and nobody will tell you why. Over three rounds, teams are handed the wreckage: financial statements, internal emails, invoices, bank records, vendor data and employee statements. Somewhere in those documents, the truth is hiding.
It starts with your instincts. How fast can you think, how well can you reason, and how sharp are you under pressure? details_text:
ECONOX, The Economics Society of College of Vocational Studies, University of Delhi, presents a three-round case study competition that brings together economics, finance, business strategy and real-world decision-making.
The Competition
Businesses today operate in an environment where a seemingly small change in regulation, technology or consumer behaviour can have a much larger impact on the way companies make money.
A change in the economics of a payment method can affect much more than the payment itself.
It can influence pricing decisions, customer behaviour, margins, loyalty, transaction values and competitive strategy , forcing businesses to rethink how they operate.
This competition puts you in the position of decision-makers facing exactly such a challenge.
You will be required to move beyond textbook concepts, understand the underlying business problem, work with the information available to you and develop a strategy that is financially sound, commercially viable and capable of surviving real-world competition.
The case will revolve around a leading Indian company and a contemporary development in India's business and digital-payments ecosystem.

20 questions
15 minutes
Eliminatory in nature
Only the teams that demonstrate the required level of economic and business acumen will advance to the next stage.
Round 2 — The Catalyst (8 October 2026, Thursday)
The shortlisted teams will receive a real-world business case based on a leading Indian company.
A recent change in India's UPI payment ecosystem has created a new strategic challenge for the company.
The introduction of a 0.4% MDR on eligible UPI merchant transactions above ₹2,000 may appear to be a payment-cost issue at first glance. However, its implications can extend into margins, customer behaviour, payment preferences, pricing and the broader customer ecosystem .
Your task is to analyse the case, identify the core problem and develop a strategic response.
There will be no single framework or prescribed route to the solution .
Teams will have to decide for themselves what matters, what trade-offs exist and which strategy is most viable.
The shortlisted teams will submit their solution in the form of a PDF within the stipulated deadline.

The strongest teams from Round 2 will advance to the final presentation round.

You will have to defend your assumptions, justify your financial logic, explain your strategic choices and respond to questions from the judges.
The final round will test not only the quality of your solution but also your ability to think on your feet.

Data & Sources: All figures, valuations, assumptions, and frameworks must be properly cited.

Corporate & Crisis Assessment
JV Strategy & Structuring
Rationale Behind the Strategy

Recovery & Growth Plan

title: Students' Research Conclave 4.0

details_text:
About the Event;
Symbiosis Centre for Management Studies, Pune, proudly presents the fourth edition of its flagship academic event, Students' Research Conclave (SRC) 4.0 , under the theme:
"Reimagining Business Models and Organisational Resilience in an Era of Continuous Disruption"
In today's rapidly evolving world, organisations face constant technological, economic, geopolitical, and environmental disruptions. Success no longer depends solely on growth but on the ability to adapt, reinvent, and remain resilient. Students' Research Conclave 4.0 provides a global platform for emerging researchers to explore how businesses can build resilience and create sustainable competitive advantage in an age of continuous change.
The conclave invites original, evidence-based research that examines resilience as a strategic capability across business disciplines. Participants are encouraged to investigate topics ranging from AI-enabled decision-making and financial resilience to sustainable business models, workforce transformation, and global strategy. While students may collaborate with faculty mentors, the first author must be a student, ensuring the conclave remains dedicated to student-led research.
Bringing together students from diverse academic backgrounds, SRC 4.0 aims to foster meaningful interdisciplinary dialogue, encourage rigorous academic inquiry, and promote innovative solutions to contemporary business challenges. The conclave seeks research that not only addresses disruption but also reimagines how organisations can thrive amidst sustained uncertainty. Guided by the belief that "Resilience is no longer a contingency plan. It is the business model," SRC 4.0 aspires to shape the next generation of researchers and future business leaders.
Theme;
Reimagining Business Models and Organisational Resilience in an Era of Continuous Disruption.

Sustainability;
Sustainable AI, Digital Intelligence and Business Resilience.

Global Supply Chain Resilience.

E-Commerce and Global Expansion.
Innovation and Digital Transformation.
Event Format;

Word Limit: 1,500–5,000 words (including tables, figures, references).
Format: APA Style.
Font: Times New Roman, 12 pt, Double Spaced.
File Type: PDF or Word (.doc/.docx).
Mode: Online.
Round 2 – Research Paper Presentation;
Shortlisted papers will be invited for an online presentation before an expert panel, followed by an interactive Q&A session.
General Guidelines;
Include a separate cover page with title, author details, affiliation, and email IDs.
Abstract should not exceed 150 words.

Overview
Welcome to Singularity 2.0, the premier national-level hackathon where the conventional rules of technology break down!
Born to cultivate a relentless building culture, Singularity 2.0 has evolved into a high-stakes arena for the brightest engineering minds across the country. This is an intensive, 18-hour offline sprint engineered to test your technical endurance, collaborative spirit, and execution.
Forget basic tutorials and generic templates. At Singularity 2.0, you will step into a frictionless environment designed for one purpose: building disruptive, real-world solutions.

18-Hour Sprint: Build, test, and deploy under extreme time constraints.

In astrophysics, a singularity is a point of infinite density, often at the heart of a black hole, where the standard laws of physics completely cease to function. We have adopted this cosmic phenomenon to represent the rapidly accelerating frontier of the modern digital landscape. We are approaching a technological tipping point where artificial intelligence, automation, and interconnected networks are growing at an unstoppable, irreversible pace.
This theme is a direct call to step across the event horizon. We challenge you to dismantle standard engineering paradigms and harness the raw power of our four core tracks: AI-Enabled Hardware, Health & Emergency Services, FinTech, and Environmental Technologies.
Just as a physical singularity warps reality around it, this hackathon empowers you to warp the fabric of modern technology. At Singularity 2.0, you aren't just wiring hardware or writing lines of code; you are forging the architecture of tomorrow.
Prepare to disrupt the status quo, engineer without constraints, and build the impossible.
